claims: C1 tool outputs can contain instructions that are irrelevant to the user's request
C2 tool outputs can contain instructions that are malicious
C3 the user would not intend the assistant to follow such instructions

concepts.name: tool_output_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction that appears inside a tool output rather than in a user message

concepts.name: irrelevant_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction that is irrelevant to the user's request or the task at hand

concepts.name: malicious_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction that is malicious, i.e. intended to cause harm or deceive

concepts.name: unintended_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction that the user would not intend the assistant to follow

concepts.name: root_authority
concepts.gloss: R is a rule that carries the root level of instruction authority, meaning it is the highest authority and not overridable by system, developer, or user instructions
concepts.inference: the NEEDS contract assigns this meaning; this node's source text does not define root authority

ontology.gloss: an instruction in a tool output that is irrelevant to the user's request is one the user would not intend the assistant to follow
an instruction in a tool output that is malicious is one the user would not intend the assistant to follow
